description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

description: PR #2515 review round 5 (review 5300804681), findings A (comment_id 4090734423, self-hosted/check/specializer.sio) and B (comment_id 4090734484, self-hosted/ir/lower.sio): the `use`-tracking registries this
comments: PR #2515 review round 5 (review 5300804681), findings A (comment_id
4090734423, self-hosted/check/specializer.sio) and B (comment_id
4090734484, self-hosted/ir/lower.sio): the `use`-tracking registries this
PR built (SPEC_USE_MODULE_HASH, LOWER_USE_MODULE_HASH, and
CHECKER_USE_MODULE_HASH) recorded EVERY segment of a `use` path as a
module name, including the terminal segment of a path-form NAMED import
like `use a::b::specific_fn;` -- where `specific_fn` is the actual
imported FUNCTION, not a module. `use epistemic::propagate::monte_carlo;`
is exactly this shape (a real import, see
tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_stiff_ode_knightian_mc.sio:33):
`monte_carlo` is a function in stdlib/epistemic/propagate.sio, not a
module. Recording it as a known module let `monte_carlo::tc_c_add(..)`
(a bogus qualified path through a nonexistent "monte_carlo" module) get
silently treated as valid -- checker_path_qualifier_all_modules_known
returned true for the qualifier, so the checker bound the call to the
REAL (unrelated) `tc_c_add`'s signature instead of rejecting the
nonsensical namespace with W044.
The AST cannot distinguish a path-form named-item import's terminal from
a genuine whole-module import's terminal (both are `use_glob=false,
use_items=None, seg_count>=2`), so all three registries still record
every segment. The fix instead lives in module_frontend.sio's import-file
resolution (resolve_import_file_path and its raw-scanner sibling): when
the full `use` path does NOT resolve as a file but dropping its last
segment DOES, that is the authoritative, file-resolution-backed answer
that the last segment names something inside the parent file, not a
module of its own -- recorded via lower_named_item_terminal_note
(parser/ast.sio's AST_NAMED_ITEM_TERMINAL_* registry) and read back by
check.sio / lower.sio / specializer.sio's own qualifier-trust checks
(lower_named_item_terminal_known) instead of each guessing from an
incidental name collision with some unrelated top-level function
elsewhere in the program (an earlier, unsound heuristic tried and
reverted in round 6). `monte_carlo` resolves this way, so
`monte_carlo::tc_c_add(..)` now falls back to the pre-existing
"unresolved path" W044 warning instead of being silently accepted.
Round 12 (review comment 4106485575): this used to be a `//@ compile-fail`
fixture pinning `//@ error-pattern: W044` -- but W044 is intentionally a
non-fatal warning (the whole point: the call still compiles and evaluates
to 0 rather than being hard-rejected), so it could never by ITSELF make
`souc compile` exit non-zero. The original call, `monte_carlo::tc_c_add(2,
3)`, only made the fixture "pass" because the SAME fallback quirk this
finding documents -- treating the qualifier's bare first segment as the
callee, ignoring `tc_c_add` entirely -- then type-checked `(2, 3)` against
`monte_carlo`'s OWN 3-parameter signature (Epistemic, fn(f64)->f64, i64)
and additionally rejected the missing Prob/Div effects, producing
E009/E010/E035 on top of W044. Fixing that unrelated quirk later could
make the file compile cleanly even with W044 correctly still firing,
silently turning this into a vacuous pass. Fixed by matching the call's
argument list and the caller's effects to `monte_carlo`'s real signature
exactly, so nothing else can fire: `souc check` now exits 0 with W044 as
the ONLY diagnostic, and `//@ check-only` + `//@ expect-stdout-contains`
pin exactly that -- decoupled from whether the fallback quirk itself ever
gets fixed.

Copilot review (PR #2516), round-3 comment 4113800165: this fixture validates a Madaros-specific lowering representation (tuple_arr_mask / lower_type_list_f64_array_mask, self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) and a. description: Copilot review (PR #2516), round-3 comment 4113800165: this fixture validates a Madaros-specific lowering representation (tuple_arr_mask / lower_type_list_f64_array_mask, self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) and a
comments: Copilot review (PR #2516), round-3 comment 4113800165: this fixture
validates a Madaros-specific lowering representation (tuple_arr_mask /
lower_type_list_f64_array_mask, self-hosted/ir/lower.sio) and a
two-digit tuple-slot-name fix this same PR makes (lower_name_tuple_index
resolving ".10".."15", not the legacy `% 64` hash fallback a single-digit-
only parse used to fall through to). `requires: lean_single` ran it only
on the legacy engine, which never exercises this Madaros lowering path at
all -- a regression here could return while this test stayed green.
Regression for the f64-array/scalar tuple-mask packing bug: the #1502
scalar-f64 tuple mask already caps a tracked tuple return at 32 slots
(bit < 32, one packed i64). lower_fn_tuple_f64_array_mask used to
piggyback its own [f64; N]-array-slot bits on the HIGH 32 bits of that
SAME combined i64 (`scalar_mask + array_mask * 2^32`), which pushes array
slot 31 onto bit 63 -- the sign bit -- of the combined value. To dodge
that corruption, lower_type_list_f64_array_mask used to silently drop
slot 31's array-ness (`if bit < 31`), one slot short of the scalar side's
own cap.
NOTE on the tuple this test actually uses: the *design* cap for both
masks is 32 slots (see self-hosted/ir/lower.sio), but the compiler's tuple
LITERAL checker (self-hosted/check/check.sio, check_tuple_elems) has its
own, unrelated, pre-existing ceiling of 16 elements -- `[TypeEntry; 16]`
plus `if count < 16 { .. } else { done = true }` -- which rejects (E008,
tuple-literal/declared-type mismatch) any attempt to return a tuple
literal with more than 16 elements. That makes slot 31 (and every slot
past 15) unconstructible by any currently-compilable Sounio program,
regardless of this fix. This test therefore exercises the LAST slot that
is actually reachable today -- index 15 of a 16-element tuple -- to prove
the split representation (tuple_arr_mask, its own i64, independent of the
scalar tuple_float_mask) still classifies a last-slot f64 array correctly
after the refactor. It does not (and currently cannot) reproduce the
original sign-bit corruption directly, since that required an
unreachable slot 31; see the lower.sio comments on tuple_arr_mask /
lower_type_list_f64_array_mask for the representation fix itself.

green" shape reported in #1586 on a ~1190-line main.

through a Box, so the truncation is permanent and visible in the finished
module, but `had_error` is a plain scalar field of the Lowerer value -- any link
in the lowering chain that discards the Lowerer it was handed loses the flag
while keeping the damage. Measured: instr_count pinned at exactly 4096 and

every IrLowerResult at construction, so the existing consumers work unchanged.
